title: RPG2: Robust Profile-Guided Runtime Prefetch Generation
problem: Identifying which data to prefetch and when to do so is challenging; prefetches can occur too early (causing eviction of useful data) or too late (missing cache misses), while also competing for limited off-chip memory bandwidth with demand accesses.
motivation: Accurate, well-timed prefetches can dramatically improve processor performance by keeping the pipeline fed and avoiding majority of cache misses.
method: RPG2 uses profile-guided approach to generate runtime prefetch decisions that adapt to program characteristics, input, and microarchitecture. The system collects profiling information during execution to guide prefetch generation while accounting for timing constraints and bandwidth allocation between prefetches and demand accesses.
key_novelty: Demonstrates that robust prefetch generation must adapt to program input, processor microarchitecture, and their interactions rather than relying on static prefetch policies.
contributions: Handling of timing tradeoffs in prefetch insertion (early eviction vs late arrival)
Bandwidth-aware prefetch generation balancing prefetch and demand access competition
Robustness evaluation showing dependency on program input and microarchitecture

metrics.other: Robustness across program inputs and microarchitectures
